input.question: Has the addition of "Drink Responsibly" or "Winners know when to quit" in advertisements actually made any change to alcoholic and gambling addictions?
input.ground_truth: Personally, I don't know any of the statistics. But, I always thought such slogans were more to relive the companies from legal action. Like they could say "Look, we TOLD them to drink responsibly, it isn't our fault he had 20 of our beers and drove".

But, just putting a sticker on the toy doesn’t always stop someone from playing with it too much. Some people might still play or drink too much, even if they see the sticker. The sticker is there to remind people to be careful, but it doesn’t always make everyone stop or change what they do.

So, those phrases in ads try to help people remember to be careful, but they don’t always make everyone stop having problems with drinking too much or gambling too much.
